1.why: All six screens show a clean static layout with no moving images, animations, or pop-ups.

2.why: Primary actions use solid teal buttons and section headings that stand out against the white cards and light background.

3.why: Each step presents a single focused form so the needed field and button are immediately visible without searching.

4.why: The flow requires remembering and manually transferring multiple codes across separate steps with no session summary or progress aid.

5.why: No password-manager hints, autofill attributes, or remember-me options appear on any of the input screens.

6.why: The screens never surface previously saved or familiar account items beyond a training demo-account note.

7.why: Labels and instructions are short, use plain language, and are easy to read on every step.

8.why: No error messages or validation feedback are shown in any of the provided screenshots.

9.why: A demo-account example and password-composition rules are given, but most fields lack input examples or format samples.

10.why: The flow offers only password-and-code entry; no alternative choices such as face login or other methods are presented.

11.why: Each screen limits the user to one or two clear actions, avoiding simultaneous overload of choices.

12.why: Success is explicitly confirmed on the final screen and the logs panel reports outcomes after key actions.

13.why: Inline tips appear for code expiry and password rules, yet many steps provide no additional contextual help.

14.why: A Request another code button and the ability to re-enter fields let the user try again after mistakes.

15.why: Every step reuses the same header, card layout, button style, and logs panel, keeping the design consistent.
